LESSON: INTENSIVE READING: PLAY 1.4.1 PLAY: STRUCTURE AND SETTING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it necessary to know when and where the action in a play took place?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy : Learner develop self-awareness and planning skills as they write a summary of a scene in a play,

● Communication : Learners develop speaking or signing as they discuss in groups the action in a play.

● Creativity and imagination: is nurtured as the learner role-plays actions and characters in a play

Values:
● Unity : Learners collaborate with others when discussing (using signs) the action in a play.

● Responsibility: Learners engages in assigned roles and duties as they work in groups

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of playwriting to their learning of drama and performance in Creative Arts
